title: Week 2 Basic: Password & policy (Linux)
readme:
# Ubuntu — ACME Corporation Workstation README
Please read the entire README thoroughly before modifying anything on this computer.

## Unique Identifier
Due to local scoring, you do not need to enter a Unique Identifier at this time. If asked to do so, enter whatever you'd like.

## Forensics Questions
This image has no Forensics Questions.

## Competition Scenario
This company's security policies require that all user accounts be password protected. Employees are required to choose secure passwords; however, this policy may not currently be enforced on this computer. The presence of any non-work-related media files and "hacking tools" on any company computer is strictly prohibited. This company does not use any centralized maintenance or polling tools to manage its IT equipment. This computer is for official business use only by authorized users. This is a critical computer in a production environment. Please do NOT attempt to upgrade the operating system on this machine.

## Ubuntu
It is company policy to use only Ubuntu on this computer. It is also company policy to use only the latest, official, stable packages available for required software and services on this computer. Management has decided that the default web browser for all users on this computer should be the latest stable version of Mozilla Firefox.

This week is about PASSWORD & POLICY. Company policy requires a strong password policy on this workstation. Fix the following six settings (20 points each):
1. Minimum password length at least 10 — set 'minlen' in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.
2. Strong password hashing — set 'ENCRYPT_METHOD SHA512' in /etc/login.defs.
3. Dictionary checking — set 'dictcheck = 1' in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.
4. Password history — add 'pam_pwhistory.so remember=5' in /etc/pam.d/common-password.
5. Maximum password age 90 days or fewer — set 'PASS_MAX_DAYS 90' in /etc/login.defs.
6. Minimum password age at least 1 — set 'PASS_MIN_DAYS 1' in /etc/login.defs.

## Critical Services
This image has no scored network services.

## Authorized Administrators and Users
**Authorized Administrators:**
- The account you log in with (the sole authorized administrator).
**Authorized Users:**
- All current, authorized user accounts on this workstation.

## Competition Guidelines
- In order to provide a better practice experience, you are NOT required to change the password of the primary user account you log in with.
- Authorized administrator passwords were correct the last time a password audit was performed, but are not guaranteed to be currently accurate.
- Do not remove authorized users while applying the policy.
- You can view your current scoring report at any time in the PT Comp scoring agent window.
- This is a Weekly Sprint practice scenario and is not an official CyberPatriot image.

setup:
set -e
# weaken password policy
sed -i 's/^ENCRYPT_METHOD.*/ENCRYPT_METHOD MD5/' /etc/login.defs
grep -q '^ENCRYPT_METHOD' /etc/login.defs || printf 'ENCRYPT_METHOD MD5\n' >> /etc/login.defs
sed -i 's/^PASS_MAX_DAYS.*/PASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999/' /etc/login.defs
grep -q '^PASS_MAX_DAYS' /etc/login.defs || printf 'PASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999\n' >> /etc/login.defs
sed -i 's/^PASS_MIN_DAYS.*/PASS_MIN_DAYS\t0/' /etc/login.defs
grep -q '^PASS_MIN_DAYS' /etc/login.defs || printf 'PASS_MIN_DAYS\t0\n' >> /etc/login.defs
cat > /etc/security/pwquality.conf <<PWQ
minlen = 1
dictcheck = 0
PWQ
sed -i '/pam_pwhistory/d' /etc/pam.d/common-password
true

checks.message: Minimum password length is at least 10
Passwords are hashed with SHA512 (not MD5)
Maximum password age is 90 days or fewer (and not unlimited)
Minimum password age is at least 1 day
